title: Per-drone DDS domain vs PX4 UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID mismatch (CONFIRMED on ghost; fleet-wide invariant still unverified)
evidence: POSTMORTEM.md:16-27 (mechanism), FINDINGS.md:22 run03 PASS: 'wifi ON: VVO 29.87 Hz ... xy/z/v_xy/v_z_valid all true, nav_state 2'; broken state = zero /fmu/out/* on domain 3 while XRCE session established (run01/data/A_wifi_on/c_fmu_vehicle_status.txt, tab2_pane.txt:13); POSTMORTEM.md:58-60 invariant '1=delta,2=buckshee,3=ghost,4=thunderstrike' — param only set on ghost.
why_it_could_cause_stuck: The same silent one-way/no-way DDS partition can exist on any drone whose FMU param was never updated (only ghost was fixed). Symptom class: pipeline looks alive, agent session established, but PX4 never receives /fmu/in/* (or nodes never see /fmu/out/*) => EKF2 loses/never gets external vision, Offboard setpoint stream or offboard_control_mode heartbeats silently vanish => PX4 failsafe/hold mid-exploration = 'gets stuck'. Domain mismatch can also be re-introduced by the container recreate that lost the DDS wrapper fix.
sim_repro_idea: In AirSim/HERCULES, run the PX4-side bridge (or a stand-in XRCE agent) on ROS domain 0 while exploration/vio nodes run on domain N: verify vehicle enters Offboard, then starve /fmu/in/trajectory_setpoint + offboard_control_mode mid-exploration and observe PX4 offboard-loss failsafe => drone holds/loiters while planner keeps planning (stuck).
verify_reasoning:
Every cited file exists and says what the finding claims — the ghost-specific sub-finding is genuinely CONFIRMED by the debug artifacts. Verified: (1) POSTMORTEM.md:16-27 states the mechanism exactly as quoted (MicroXRCEAgent creates DDS entities on the domain the PX4 client requests via UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID, read once at startup, default 0; container ROS_DOMAIN_ID has no effect on the agent's entities). (2) FINDINGS.md:22 run03 PASS line matches verbatim (VVO 29.87 Hz, all validity flags true, nav_state 2). (3) Broken-state evidence is real: run01/data/A_wifi_on/c_env.txt shows ROS_DOMAIN_ID=3, c_topic_list.txt contains zero /fmu topics, c_fmu_vehicle_status.txt shows "does not appear to be published yet", and tab2_pane.txt:12-13 shows the XRCE "session established" over serial — pipeline alive, session up, PX4 invisible. (4) POSTMORTEM.md:58-64 states the fleet invariant (1=delta, 2=buckshee, 3=ghost, 4=thunderstrike) and that only ghost was fixed ("Not changed here (change discipline: ghost only)"). I additionally found corroboration the finding did not cite: all four launchers pin per-drone domains (delta=1 line 42, buckshee=2, thunderstrike=4 plus ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1), the delta launcher comment literally says "VERIFY/SET delta=1 in QGC before flying!" (unverified on delta), and the canonical fleet param files px4_params/prometheus_uav_VIO_fused_PX4_params_july-{5,15}-2025.params line 1077 still carry UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID=0 — so any FMU flashed/restored from the reference param set silently regresses to the broken state. The fleet-wide risk is therefore well-grounded, not just asserted.

Why not CONFIRMED for the stuck-in-exploration bug: the causal chain from this mismatch to the USER'S reported symptom sequence is speculative and partly inconsistent with it. A full static domain mismatch produces total /fmu/* invisibility from boot — EKF2 never gets external vision, so the drone should fail to hold Position/enter Offboard at all (exactly what ghost showed: a from-the-start failure, diagnosed on the bench, nav_state POSCTL validity as the test — no mid-flight drop). The user's symptom is a drone that arms in Position, enters Offboard, explores, THEN gets stuck — which requires the /fmu/in link to have been working. To rescue the mechanism you need either (a) a mismatched TEAMMATE drone stalling the coordinated frontier exploration of the healthy one (behavior of active_exploration/loop-closure coordination is in the unavailable private repos — inferred only), or (b) a mid-mission re-introduction via container recreate (documented as having happened once for the FASTDDS wrapper, but no evidence it occurs mid-flight; UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID lives in FMU flash, not the container, so container recreate does not change the domain the PX4 client requests — it could only re-break the separate agent-binding/profiles issue). So: real, file-confirmed failure mechanism and a legitimate fleet-wide reproduction candidate for AirSim, but its identification as THE cause of the mid-exploration stall is unproven.
corrected_evidence: All original citations verified accurate: POSTMORTEM.md:16-27 (mechanism), POSTMORTEM.md:58-64 (invariant + ghost-only fix + thunderstrike warning), FINDINGS.md:22 (run03 PASS quote verbatim), ghost_debug/run01/data/A_wifi_on/{c_env.txt:3 ROS_DOMAIN_ID=3, c_topic_list.txt zero /fmu entries, c_fmu_vehicle_status.txt "does not appear to be published yet", tab2_pane.txt:12-13 "session established"}. Strengthening evidence to ADD: (1) launch_delta_frontierexplore_tmux.sh:39-41 comment "VERIFY/SET delta=1 in QGC before flying!" — explicit in-repo admission the param is unverified on delta; equivalent invariant comments at :39 of buckshee (domain 2) and thunderstrike (domain 4, which also sets ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1 per POSTMORTEM.md:61-64). (2) px4_params/prometheus_uav_VIO_fused_PX4_params_july-15-2025.params:1077 and july-5 variant: "UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID 0" — the canonical VIO-fused fleet param file carries domain 0, so restoring params from it silently re-breaks any domain-pinned drone. CORRECTION to claimed mechanism: "re-introduced by the container recreate" conflates two bugs — UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID persists in FMU flash and is untouched by container recreate; the recreate-loss risk applies to the separate FASTDDS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE agent-binding wrapper, while domain mismatch is re-introduced by FMU param restore/reflash from the reference .params files. CAVEAT: a static domain mismatch on the flying drone is inconsistent with the reported arm→Offboard→stuck sequence (it fails before Offboard entry, as ghost did); the mismatch fits the user symptom only as a mismatched-teammate coordination stall, which depends on unavailable private-repo behavior (inferred).

title: cuVSLAM frame-time stutter + non-monotonic timestamp error present even in the healthy baseline
evidence: run03/data/tab1_pane.txt:325-345: 'Delta between frame is 468 ms ... longer than desired 34 ms', 'Lost IMU msgs: 88 ... drop ratio = 100%', '[ERROR] CUVSLAM_INVALID_ARG(2U) Condition failed: some_image.timestamp_ns >= tracker->last_timestamp_ns'; VVO max gap 0.061 s even when passing (run03/data/hz_vvo.txt).
why_it_could_cause_stuck: Under exploration load (nvblox + FIS + planner + zenoh + SuperPoint/LightGlue all on one Orin NX), these bench-visible stutters grow: VIO gaps >~200 ms or a timestamp regression can make EKF2 EV timeout/reset, flipping xy_valid false mid-Offboard => position-hold/failsafe => exploration halts. This is the strongest bench-observed precursor of an in-flight VIO glitch.
sim_repro_idea: In sim, inject odometry dropouts (100-500 ms gaps) and occasional backwards-timestamped VVO messages into /fmu/in/vehicle_visual_odometry during exploration; observe EKF2 EV rejection, local_position validity flags dropping, and planner/guard behavior when odometry freezes.
verify_reasoning: Evidence is real; causal mechanism is speculative extrapolation. VERIFIED: (1) All quoted lines exist in run03/data/tab1_pane.txt — lines 331-334 '[WARNING] Delta between frame is 468 ms that is longer than desired 34 ms' + 'Lost IMU msgs: 88, Frame time delta = 0.467556 [s], drop ratio = 100.000000 [%]', and lines 335-336 '[ERROR] CUVSLAM_INVALID_ARG(2U) Condition failed: some_image.timestamp_ns >= tracker->last_timestamp_ns'. (2) hz_vvo.txt confirms VVO ~29.87 Hz with max gap 0.061 s. (3) run03 is genuinely the healthy baseline: FINDINGS.md line 22 marks run03 'PASS — root cause confirmed, GOAL met'. REFUTING CONTEXT THE FINDING OMITS: the big stutters (66-851 ms deltas, lines ~212-660) and the single CUVSLAM_INVALID_ARG error are confined to the startup window (~01:09:55-01:10:30), during which the RealSense node was failing to claim the USB device (lines 363-379: 'failed to claim usb interface... RS2_USB_STATUS_BUSY', 'requested device with is NOT found. Will Try again') and nvblox was allocating GPU memory pools. A 14,598 ms frame gap at line 1542 ends exactly at 'RealSense Node Is Up!' (01:10:30) — i.e., the camera was restarting. After that, frame deltas are a clean 33-34 ms through end-of-log; only small 'Lost IMU msgs: 2-6' warnings persist in steady state. So the bench data shows a camera-bringup/USB-contention transient, NOT steady-state stutter, and cuVSLAM visibly survived the timestamp regression (tracking continued; FINDINGS.md line 26 calls the vision pipeline healthy at IMU 200 Hz / cuVSLAM 30 Hz / VVO 30 Hz). THE CLAIMED MECHANISM (exploration load grows gaps >200 ms → EKF2 EV timeout/reset → xy_valid false → failsafe → exploration halts) is internally consistent with PX4 EKF2 behavior but has zero direct file evidence: run03 never ran the full exploration load (no FIS/planner/SuperPoint active in the bench log), no log shows an EKF2 EV timeout, xy_valid flip, or failsafe event, and the load-sensitivity of the stutter is contradicted by its correlation with USB contention rather than compute. Behavior of active_exploration/px4_offboard is inferred (private repos unavailable). Worth reproducing in AirSim as one candidate (inject VIO gaps/timestamp regression and observe EKF2), but it cannot be CONFIRMED as the stuck-exploration root cause from these files.
corrected_evidence: run03/data/tab1_pane.txt lines 331-336 (not 325-345) contain the 468 ms delta, Lost-IMU-88, and CUVSLAM_INVALID_ARG timestamp-regression error — all within the startup window where the RealSense node was retrying USB claims (lines 45-49 and 363-379: RS2_USB_STATUS_BUSY, 'device NOT found. Will Try again') and nvblox was initializing. Line 1542's 14,598 ms gap terminates at 'RealSense Node Is Up!' (camera restart at 01:10:30); thereafter frame deltas are 33-34 ms for the remaining ~1,200 log lines, with only small persistent 'Lost IMU msgs: 2-6' warnings. hz_vvo.txt (29.87 Hz avg, max gap 0.061 s) reflects this post-startup steady state. Corrected claim: the healthy baseline shows a startup-phase camera/USB-contention transient producing >200 ms VIO gaps and one non-monotonic-timestamp error that cuVSLAM survived, plus low-grade IMU message loss in steady state — a bench-observed precursor pattern worth simulating, but not evidence of steady-state stutter under load.

title: Stale-process contamination across relaunches (duplicate stacks, camera busy, serial port held, memory pressure)
evidence: run01 phase B: two concurrent stacks (B_radio_off/c_pgrep.txt shows PID sets 13235-15046 AND 21697-22936), camera dead ('/camera0/imu does not appear to be published yet', B_radio_off/c_hz_camera_imu.txt), RAM 12.6/15.6 GB (B_radio_off/tegrastats.txt); run03 startup RS2_USB_STATUS_BUSY / 'failed to set power state' from leftovers (run03/data/tab1_pane.txt:44-62); clean_ghost.sh:2-3 'tmux kill alone leaves docker-exec'd processes alive — the agent keeps /dev/ttyUSB0'; FINDINGS.md:44-46 pkill self-match lesson.
why_it_could_cause_stuck: The real launchers use the same tmux/docker-exec mechanics. A partially-killed previous run leaves a second vio_bridge/agent publishing stale /fmu/in/* (or holding /dev/ttyUSB0 so the new agent gets no PX4 link), and doubles RAM/CPU load on a 16 GB Orin — intermittent 'launches fine, then errors/stalls during exploration' behavior that depends on what survived the previous kill. Also relevant: radiohive's default serial /dev/ttyUSB0@57600 vs agent 921600 is the same held-port collision class.
sim_repro_idea: Run two publishers on /fmu/in/vehicle_visual_odometry (or two setpoint writers) with slightly different poses in sim and observe EKF/controller behavior; separately simulate agent losing serial mid-run (kill XRCE link) during Offboard.
verify_reasoning:
Every cited file exists and every quote is accurate, and the contamination PHENOMENON is directly evidenced; but the causal link to the user's stuck-during-frontier-exploration symptom is extrapolated, and one sub-attribution ('run03 busy from leftovers') is not proven by the files.

VERIFIED REAL: (1) run01/data/B_radio_off/c_pgrep.txt shows exactly two concurrent full stacks — PIDs 13235/13256/13270/13272/14960/15020/15046 and 21697/21756/21797/21799/22826/22905/22934/22936 — including TWO concurrent vio_bridge binaries (15046, 22936), so 'second vio_bridge publishing /fmu/in/*' is evidenced. (2) c_hz_camera_imu.txt is exactly 'WARNING: topic [/camera0/imu] does not appear to be published yet'. (3) tegrastats.txt shows RAM 12644/15656MB (swap 0 used). (4) run03/data/tab1_pane.txt lines 44-63 (recurring at 363-382 and 649-668) show 'failed to claim usb interface... RS2_USB_STATUS_BUSY' / 'acquire_power failed: failed to set power state'. (5) clean_ghost.sh lines 2-3 verbatim: 'tmux kill alone leaves docker-exec'd processes alive — the agent keeps /dev/ttyUSB0'. (6) FINDINGS.md lines 44-46 document the pkill self-match lesson. (7) The 'same mechanics' claim holds: launch_ghost_frontierexplore_tmux.sh line 101 launches via tmux + docker exec, and its kill mode (lines 179-181) is ONLY 'tmux kill-server' with no in-container pkill — combined with clean_ghost.sh's empirical note, the production teardown path is directly shown to be insufficient, leaving the XRCE agent holding /dev/ttyUSB0.

WHY NOT CONFIRMED: (a) The run01-B duplicate stack was self-inflicted by the DEBUG harness's un-bracketed pkill killing its own shell (FINDINGS.md line 20, POSTMORTEM Ops lessons) — it demonstrates the contamination class but is not an observation of the production launchers doing this in normal use. (b) The run03 USB-busy attribution to 'leftovers' is weakened by run03/test.sh lines 21-34, which hard-killed with the bracket trick and looped on pgrep until zero BEFORE launching — yet busy errors still appeared; the files never identify what held the device (circumstantially a stale holder existed, since visual_slam_node was receiving frames — 'Delta between current and previous frame' warnings from ~line 153 — while its own camera node could not claim USB, and the leftover-procs count output was not saved; note odom_correction is absent from every pkill pattern list). (c) No captured run ever executed the exploration stack (active_exploration, octomap_exchange, loop-closure, radiohive were not among the pgrep'd processes), so 'stalls DURING exploration' from doubled load/held serial is inference about unavailable private-repo behavior, not observed. (d) The one fully debugged incident in these files had a different root cause (ROS_DOMAIN_ID=3 vs UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID=0 mismatch, POSTMORTEM.md), and run03 PASSED (VVO 29.87 Hz) despite the recurring USB-busy warnings — so contamination present in the data did not, in that instance, produce the stall. (e) Memory: 12.6/15.6 GB with zero swap used, captured with only 2x(vslam+nvblox+vio_bridge) and no exploration nodes; 'memory pressure causes the stall' is untested extrapolation.

Net: a real, file-documented failure class that the production launchers' kill path provably does not clean up, and a legitimate reproduction candidate for intermittent post-relaunch weirdness — but its role as the cause of the frontier-exploration stall is speculative, per the PLAUSIBLE criterion.
corrected_evidence: Corrections/refinements to the cited evidence: (1) run03 tab1_pane.txt busy block is lines 44-63, not 44-62, and recurs at lines 363-382 and 649-668 (~every 6s retry). (2) run01 B_radio_off/c_pgrep.txt: only the SECOND stack has a MicroXRCEAgent (PID 22934, 'MicroXRCEAgent serial --dev /dev/ttyUSB0 -b 921600'); the first stack's vio_bridge launch (15020) shows no agent — so the file shows two vio_bridge processes but NOT two agents contending for ttyUSB0. (3) The run01-B duplication was caused by the debug harness's own pkill self-match (FINDINGS.md line 20: 'B-phase contaminated (cleanup pkill self-match killed its own shell → two stacks ran concurrently)'), not by the production launcher. (4) run03's busy errors occurred DESPITE run03/test.sh lines 21-34 hard-killing (bracket-trick pkill of MicroXRCEAgent/vio_bridge/component_container/ros2-launch) and waiting for pgrep count 0 before launch; the leftover attribution is circumstantial — supported only by visual_slam_node receiving frames (frame-delta warnings from ~line 153, 'Frame time delta = 4205.75 s' first-frame gap) while its camera node could not claim the USB device, implying some unidentified holder/publisher; odom_correction is missing from all pkill patterns. (5) Strongest new supporting evidence not in the original citation: launch_ghost_frontierexplore_tmux.sh lines 179-181 — the production 'kill' mode is solely 'tmux kill-server 2>/dev/null', with no in-container pkill; per clean_ghost.sh lines 2-3 this leaves docker-exec'd processes (including the agent holding /dev/ttyUSB0) alive, so the production teardown-relaunch cycle is directly shown to be exposed to this contamination class. (6) tegrastats also shows SWAP 0/7828MB used at RAM 12644/15656MB, i.e. not yet under actual memory pressure in the captured state, and no exploration/coordination nodes (active_exploration, octomap_exchange, loop_closure, radiohive) were running in any captured pgrep — the memory/stall link is extrapolation. (7) FINDINGS.md/POSTMORTEM.md attribute the one debugged failure to the DDS domain mismatch, and run03 PASSED (VVO 29.87 Hz, nav_state POSITION) despite the recurring RS2_USB_STATUS_BUSY warnings.

title: Campaign boundary: exploration/zenoh/LoRa layers were never exercised — its PASS does not clear the current symptom
evidence: run01/data/A_wifi_on/c_node_list.txt (11 nodes, none from active_exploration/zenoh/radiohive); run03/test.sh launches only realsense_example.launch.py + vio_bridge.launch.py; run03 verdict criteria stop at bench POSITION-mode readiness (run03/test.sh:52-77); vehicle_status shows arming_state 1 = never armed in any capture.
why_it_could_cause_stuck: The ghost campaign is ground truth for the VIO->EKF2 link only. Everything downstream of Offboard entry (frontier clustering, planner setpoints, reactive_depth_guard as sole /fmu/in writer, zenoh+LoRa contention — including the /dev/ttyUSB0@57600 radiohive default colliding with the agent's /dev/ttyUSB0@921600) is untested by these runs and remains the open space where the current stuck-during-exploration failure lives.
sim_repro_idea: Treat run03's flag set (nav_state 2, all validity true, VVO ~30 Hz) as the 'healthy at Offboard entry' precondition in sim, then fault-inject only exploration/coordination-layer failures on top of it.
verify_reasoning: Every factual leg of the finding checks out against the files, and the mechanism is a boundary/scope claim that the file evidence directly supports — it does not depend on the unavailable private repos. (1) /home/lucas/hercules-sim/src/multirobot_launch_scripts/ghost_debug/run01/data/A_wifi_on/c_node_list.txt contains exactly 11 nodes (/camera0/camera, realsense_splitter_node, launch_ros_13256, nvblox_container, nvblox_node, odom_correction, two transform_listeners, vio_bridge, visual_slam_node, vslam_container) — nothing from active_exploration, zenoh, or radiohive, and a grep for zenoh|radiohive|lora|exploration|frontier across all of ghost_debug/ hits only the launcher filename in comments, never a running process or topic. (2) run03/test.sh launches only realsense_example.launch.py (line 39) and vio_bridge.launch.py (line 42); it never launches exploration, the offboard mission, or any radio link. (3) The verdict criteria (metric capture lines 52-61, verdict block lines 63-77) are: count of /fmu/out topics > 0 AND xy_valid true, with the PASS message "check POSITION mode in QGC now" — i.e., bench POSITION-mode readiness, exactly as claimed; Offboard/arming is never tested. (4) run03/data/vehicle_status.txt line 4 shows arming_state: 1 (PX4 ARMING_STATE_DISARMED; ARMED=2) with armed_time: 0 and nav_state: 2 (POSCTL) — never armed. In run01 both A/B c_fmu_vehicle_status.txt captures show vehicle_status not published at all (that was the bug under investigation), so no capture in the campaign ever shows an armed vehicle. (5) FINDINGS.md and POSTMORTEM.md confirm the campaign's scope was solely the VIO->EKF2/DDS-domain link (root cause: ROS_DOMAIN_ID=3 vs UXRCE_DDS_DOM_ID=0 mismatch, fixed by setting the PX4 param to 3). Therefore the campaign's PASS certifies only VVO delivery and EKF2 EV fusion up to Position-mode readiness; frontier clustering, planner setpoints, reactive_depth_guard's /fmu/in writes in Offboard, zenoh bridge traffic, and the radiohive /dev/ttyUSB0@57600-vs-agent@921600 collision were all outside the tested envelope. The one caveat: the closing clause that the current stuck failure "lives" in that untested space is a scoping statement (the failure occurs during exploration, which was untested), not a positive root-cause claim — as written, the finding does not overreach.

In run01 (both A_wifi_on and B_radio_off), c_fmu_vehicle_status.txt shows /fmu/out/vehicle_status was not published at all, which is even stronger evidence the vehicle was never armed in those runs. title: Re-attaching a fleet window bounces the zenoh bridge mid-flight (kill-before-start runs on EVERY Enter)
evidence: launch_fleet_tmux.sh:51-53: REMOTE="${DOCKER_UP}mkdir -p $LOGDIR; "; [ -n "$ZENOH" ] && REMOTE+="$ZENOH; " — the ZENOH string from fleet_ctl zenoh_line (fleet_ctl:156-161) begins with 'tmux kill-session -t zenoh; ... pkill -f [z]enoh-bridge-ros2dds; sleep 1; tmux new-session -d -s zenoh ...'. It is prepended UNCONDITIONALLY, before the 'tmux has-session -t fleet ||' guard, so re-running the window after an SSH drop (the documented recovery action, lines 8-15) kills and restarts the live zenoh bridge while the flight stack keeps running.
why_it_could_cause_stuck: Every re-attach (common on flaky field WiFi) causes a multi-second zenoh outage plus a fresh bridge with new DDS discovery. Loop-closure and octomap-exchange peers see peer topics vanish/reappear; if those nodes block on a peer response, hold stale alignment state, or the frontier planner waits on merged-map updates, exploration stalls exactly 'while coordinating over the zenoh bridge'. Discovery churn can also leave the new bridge half-connected (matched pub, no sub).
sim_repro_idea: In AirSim/HERCULES multi-drone run, script the zenoh-bridge-ros2dds process on one drone to be SIGKILLed and restarted (with 1s gap) mid-exploration at random intervals; observe whether loop_closure/octomap_exchange and the frontier planner recover or wedge.
corrected_evidence: launch_fleet_tmux.sh:50-53: `LOGDIR="$WS/experiment_logs"; REMOTE="${DOCKER_UP}mkdir -p $LOGDIR; "; [ -n "$ZENOH" ] && REMOTE+="$ZENOH; "` — ZENOH appended before the fleet has-session guard (lines 54-61), executed on every Enter (read prompt at line 48). fleet_ctl:149-161 zenoh_line returns `tmux kill-session -t zenoh 2>/dev/null; echo <pw> | sudo -S -p '' pkill -f '[z]enoh-bridge-ros2dds'; sleep 1; tmux new-session -d -s zenoh "... launch_bench_zenoh.sh <vid> <ip> <peers> >> /tmp/zenoh_tmux.log 2>&1"`; non-None whenever peers exist (any multi-drone flight). ADDITIONS: (a) fleet_ctl:215-223 (cmd_start) duplicates the same kill-before-start, so `fleet_ctl start` / `--headless` re-invocation mid-flight bounces ALL drones' bridges simultaneously; (b) CORRECTION: the `attach` subcommand documented at line 9 (implemented lines 76-81) is a bare `tmux attach -t fleet` and does NOT bounce zenoh — only the "re-run the window" recovery path (lines 13-15) does; (c) launch_bench_zenoh.sh is in the private multi_drone_nvblox repo (fleet_ctl:36-37), so bridge startup time/config beyond the explicit `sleep 1` is inferred; (d) no cited log/ghost_debug evidence shows a mid-flight re-run actually occurred during the failing flights.

title: fleet_ctl stop with no/typo'd drone name sweeps ALL FOUR drones with pkill -9 — mid-flight kill of the sole offboard setpoint writer
evidence: fleet_ctl:91-95: vehicles() returns list(FLEET) when 'all' in names OR NOT NAMES — i.e. './fleet_ctl stop' bare, or './fleet_ctl stop gost' (typo filtered out), stops every drone. cmd_stop (fleet_ctl:226-246) then pkill -9's '[r]os2 launch', '[c]omponent_container', '[_]node.py', '[v]io_bridge', '[M]icroXRCEAgent' inside the container and zenoh on the host of each.
why_it_could_cause_stuck: Killing reactive_depth_guard (matched by both '[r]os2 launch' and '[_]node.py' patterns) stops the /fmu/in/offboard_control_mode + trajectory_setpoint stream -> PX4 offboard failsafe on the still-flying drone; killing MicroXRCEAgent drops VIO fusion. An operator stopping 'the other drone' during a two-drone sortie can silently kill the flying one. Also '[_]node.py' is extremely broad (matches any *_node.py, including loop_closure_sp_node.py on a drone you meant to leave alone only if named — but bare 'stop' hits all).
sim_repro_idea: During a two-drone AirSim exploration run, SIGKILL the guard/planner/agent processes on one drone (emulating cmd_stop) and verify the observed failure signature matches the field 'stuck + errors' (offboard timeout, RTL/hold, planner wedged awaiting odom).
verify_reasoning: Re-read fleet_ctl. Lines 91-95 match the quote exactly: vehicles() returns list(FLEET) when 'all' in names OR not names, and names is pre-filtered to valid FLEET keys — so bare './fleet_ctl stop' and typo'd './fleet_ctl stop gost' both resolve to all four drones with no warning, prompt, or unknown-name error. cmd_stop (lines 226-246) matches exactly: per drone it kills tmux sessions, pkill's zenoh-bridge-ros2dds on the host, then inside the container runs pkill -9 -f on '[r]os2 launch', '[c]omponent_container', '[_]node.py', '[l]ora_bridge', '[v]io_bridge', '[M]icroXRCEAgent'. The causal endpoint is directly supported without touching private repos: '[M]icroXRCEAgent' is an unambiguous match, and AGENT_HANDOFF.md (lines 221-223, 251) confirms the agent is the sole serial transport for /fmu/in/offboard_control_mode and /fmu/in/trajectory_setpoint — killing it on a flying drone stops the offboard keepalive stream at PX4 (offboard stream-timeout failsafe) and drops EV fusion; '[v]io_bridge' is likewise a direct kill.
